name: Peter
role: Fisherman, apostle, and leader of the first church
summary: Simon son of John (Matthew has son of Jonah), a Galilean fisherman called by Jesus with his brother Andrew. Named Cephas, Peter, “rock”, he confessed Jesus as the Christ, denied him three times, was restored, and led the church in Jerusalem. Two letters bear his name.
body: Jesus calls him from his nets beside the Sea of Galilee and gives him the name Cephas, Aramaic for rock, which Peter translates into Greek. He is named first in every list of the Twelve and is one of the three with Jesus at the transfiguration and in Gethsemane.

He walks on the water and begins to sink; he confesses, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God”; he swears he will never fall away, and that night denies three times that he knows Jesus. By the Sea of Galilee the risen Jesus asks him three times, “Do you love Me?” and tells him, “Feed My sheep”, and how he will die.

In Acts he preaches at Pentecost, heals, is jailed and freed by an angel, and at Cornelius's house learns that “God does not show favoritism,” baptizing the first Gentile converts. Paul records opposing him to his face at Antioch over eating with Gentiles.

moments.text: Walks on the water, and sinks

later.text: First Clement, written from Rome ≈AD 96, speaks of his martyrdom without naming the place; Dionysius of Corinth (quoted by Eusebius) says Peter and Paul died in Italy at the same time, and Tertullian puts his death in Rome under Nero. Otto Zwierlein (2009) argues that none of these rests on knowledge of the event. See the card on Peter's death.

sources.title: Review of Otto Zwierlein, Petrus in Rom (2009)
sources.author: Pieter W. van der Horst

later.text: He was crucified head downward, at his own request.
traditions: Origen, as quoted by Eusebius (Church History 3.1)

later.text: Papias says Mark was Peter's interpreter and wrote down what he remembered.
